name: 1625 Prairie Avenue — Hugh J. McBirney's Tudor stone front, K01 frontage assembly

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the K01 main body at its north (low-v) side: the draft's origin moved 0.12 m north along its own frame, onto the north side of the 1911 sheet's traced main part (s20fp-1625-b1), the party wall with 1623, through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.607 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs south.
placement.symbolic_location: 1625 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1625 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1625-b1) in the lot frame: the stone front's face at 19.45 m from the rear of the trace (3.79 m from the street line), the north wall on the party line with 1623 at v -0.12 and the south wall at 7.48, so 19.45 m deep and 7.6 m along the front — the trace's own width, where the draft's 0.25 m cell fit stopped at 6.75 m. The four-storey rear section the sheet draws stepping 1.3 m further south over the rear 7.6 m (s20-1625-a1) is not built: a K01 rear wing stands behind the main body inside its width, and this one stands beside it (T-2435).

stories.note: '3½B' on the 1911 sheet (the census's re-reading of the register's '3B', its half-storey glyph): three storeys over a basement and a half storey in the roof. The 1890 photograph agrees: three storeys of windows and an attic lit by three lights in the front gable.

construction.note: The photograph shows a street front of rock-faced coursed stone and a south side wall of brick; the 1911 sheet says only 'brick'. The Tribune's 'red stone' (quoted by chicagology, not yet a source record) is the stone.

principal_floor_m.note: The ground floor stands near grade: the photograph's entrance is reached by two low steps from the walk, and its ground-floor sills sit about 1.1 m over grade (the Tribune's 'entrance at ground level', quoted by chicagology). 0.45 m, three risers.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, ground storey first. Through the photograph's camera (inland_architect_front.json, 38.6 px/m at the front's plane) the first-floor sills read at 4.15 m and the second-floor sills at 7.77 m over grade and the gable's lights at 11.6 m, so the floors at about 3.6, 7.2 and 11.0 m. The photograph's side wall rises to about 13 m before its eave, a knee wall under the attic the K01 hip cannot carry: the eave is built at the third floor (11.0 m).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1619's and 1634's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays; the photograph's south wall is brick of a lighter tone than the stone.

stone_front.note: The photograph draws the front in rock-faced coursed stone of irregular course heights, with dressed quoined surrounds at the windows and a plain plinth; K02's brownstone, rock-faced, over one base course: the Tribune's 'red stone' (quoted by chicagology; 'Prentice' brownstone in its gloss) is a brown or red sandstone. The quoined window surrounds are not built (T-2435); the south corner's quoins are not built either, the K01 measure returning them only at its low-v end, which here is the party wall.

street_front_trim.note: Flat stone lintels over every front opening: the photograph's ground- and first-floor lights stand under flat heads in dressed surrounds. Its second-floor heads are segmental and the four-light window over the door carries a hood mould (T-2435).

wall_head.note: No cornice: the photograph carries the front up as a coped wall gable and runs the south wall's eave plain, with no brackets or entablature.

roof_form.note: A pitched roof: the photograph's main roof rises behind the front gable with its ridge running back from the street, slated, with a dormer on its south slope. K01's hip, its ridge along the plan's depth, is the honest stand-in until K01 can raise the front as a wall gable (T-2428's component, T-2435).

roof_pitch_deg.note: 45 degrees, the K01 contract's steepest hip: the photograph's gable is about 57 degrees.

eave_overhang_m.note: A plain eave, short: the photograph shows the south wall's eave with little projection.

stair_tread_m.note: Two or three low steps up from the walk.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A shallow landing before a door set at grade.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the south end of the front, in the frontispiece, as the photograph shows it. 'north' is K01's name for the high-v end of the front; on the east side of the avenue the plan's v runs south, so that end is the south end on the ground.

front_bays.note: Three bays across the 7.6 m front, low v (north) to high v (south), read through the photograph's camera: the north part's two windows a storey (centred about 1.0 and 2.9-3.5 m from the party wall; the photograph's second-floor windows stand a little south of those under them, which K01's single bay line cannot follow) and the frontispiece's centre at 5.75 m, the door under one window a storey.

bays.note: None: the photograph's front is flat, its frontispiece standing proud of the north part by only a few centimetres (T-2435).

side_bays.note: None: the house's NORTH side wall (K01's 'south', low v) is the party wall with 1623, built blank, as the sheet draws the group attached.

north_bays.note: Windows in the house's SOUTH side wall (K01's 'north', high v; s from the rear), toward the open ground the sheet leaves south of 1625: the photograph shows single windows a storey along the main part's south wall, the nearest about 2 m behind the front. Their places further back are reconstructed.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall; no picture shows it.

rear_wings.note: None built: the sheet's four-storey rear section (s20-1625-a1) stands beside the main body's rear part, stepping out to the south, which a K01 rear wing (behind the main body, inside its width) cannot; the photograph shows it under a mansard with a dormer and a stack. Open for T-2435.

sash_by_storey.note: Storey by storey, the photograph's north-part windows through its camera: ground-floor lights 1.1-2.7 m over grade, first-floor 4.15-6.4 m, second-floor 7.8-10.1 m; their widths are the K01 contract's single sash (0.75-1.15 m), where the photograph's lower windows are two lights under a transom about 0.95 m across over all.

basement_lights.note: Low basement lights under the ground-floor windows: the sheet prints a basement ('B'), and a K01 front without its own openings row carries area lights. The photograph shows a plain plinth there; T-2435 weighs it.

roof_covering.note: Slate: the photograph's roof slopes and the rear section's mansard read as slate. The Tribune's 'Roman tile' (quoted by chicagology) may be the roof or the walling; K04's terracotta tile is documented-only, so it waits for a source record.

dormer.note: One pedimented dormer on the front's centre line lighting the attic, its sash at the height of the photograph's gable lights (about 11.5-13.1 m against 11.6-13.4 m). A stand-in: the photograph's gable is the whole front carried up about 7.7 m over the third floor at about 57 degrees, coped, with three lights and an oculus; the K01 hip's ridge stands 3.8 m over the eave and a dormer may not rise past it, so T-2435 replaces this dormer with the wall gable.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks: one against the north party wall, where the photograph's tall stack rises beside the gable (built behind the dormer, the photograph's stands nearer the front), and one over the rear part's south side, where the photograph's rear stack stands.

rainwater.note: Half-round gutters and round downpipes at the front's two corners: the photograph shows a downpipe down the front's north edge, against the neighbour, and one at the south corner.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit's two-over-two sash: the photograph's leaded, mullioned and transomed lights and its one-over-one segmental sash are kinds the K01 wall does not cut yet (T-2435).

entrance_kit.note: K07's panelled door at the head of a short stoop; the front yard is 3.78 m, the sheet's front at 19.45 m against the street line at 23.24 m. The photograph's doorway is flat-headed in a dressed surround under a carved panel (T-2435).

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3½B brick dwelling (D), the south unit of the group'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: 'Residence for Hugh J. McBirney, Chicago. Burling & Whitehouse, Architects.' Plate, The Inland Architect and News Record (Chicago), vol. 14 no. 8, January 1890. Photograph of the newly finished house. Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, the 1625 S. Prairie page (uncaptioned); the Art Institute of Chicago's Ryerson & Burnham Archives hold the plate (Archival Image Collection, catalogued at 1736 S. Prairie).
what_it_supplies: the front's composition: a north part two windows wide and a south frontispiece with the entrance, one window over it each storey
three storeys and an attic under a steep front wall gable, the ground floor at grade
the openings' kinds, places and proportions: mullioned and transomed lights, segment-headed sash, the flat-headed entrance and its carved panel
the rock-faced coursed stone of the front and the brick of the south side wall
the stacks, the rear section's mansard and dormers, the picket fence
what_it_does_not_supply: the plan: the 1911 Sanborn sheet's trace controls it
colour (the Tribune's 'red stone' is quoted, not yet a source record)
the north party wall, the rear and anything the house lost or gained between 1889 and 1904

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2432 (piece 1 of T-1869) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id from the house's one photograph, the Inland Architect plate of January 1890, 'Residence for Hugh J. McBirney' by Burling & Whitehouse (inland_architect_1890_01_mcbirney_residence), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20, which controls the plan. The main body is rebuilt on the K01 frontage assembly at the sheet's own width (7.6 m, where the draft's fit had stopped at 6.75 m): a K02 rock-faced brownstone street front on K03 brick sides and rear, three storeys with the ground floor near grade, the north part two windows wide and the entrance at the south end of the front under one window a storey, as the photograph composes it; a slated K04/K05 hip with a pedimented dormer on the front marking where the photograph's steep wall gable stands. What the photograph shows and K01 cannot yet build — the full-width wall gable with its three lights and oculus, the mullioned and transomed lights, the frontispiece and its carved panel, the four-storey rear section stepping out to the south — is listed open in its match record (data/reference_views/house_1625_prairie/inland_architect_front.match.json) for T-2435. Everything not read is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1625-mcbirney-tudor-2432 (docs/RESEARCH/k01-1625-mcbirney-2432/README.md).
